a_local_prechecks.dsh_launcher_help:
Usage: dsh [options] [command] [args...]

dsh: boot a DeepSeek Harness profile — an ordered stack of plugin-bundle patch
layers under your own overrides.

Arguments:
  args                           arguments for the booted profile's app (see:
                                 dsh --profile <name> --help)

Options:
  -V, --version                  output the version number
  --profile <name>               the profile under $DSH_HOME/profiles to boot
  --from-default-profile <name>  initialize a new custom profile from a shipped
                                 profile template
  --patch <path>                 extra patch-list overlay applied after the
                                 profile layer (repeatable)
  --dump-config                  print the composed profile tree and exit
  --dump-default-config          print the profile tree without its user layer
                                 or --patch overlays and exit

Commands:
  web [options] [args...]        boot the web profile (alias of --profile web);
                                 the web app's own flags follow
  plugin [options] [args...]     manage a profile's plugins by forwarding the
                                 remaining arguments to pnpm in the profile
                                 directory

Examples:
  dsh --profile web                          boot the web profile (same as: dsh web)
  dsh --profile rescue --from-default-profile web
                                             create rescue from the shipped web template, then boot it
  dsh --profile headless "run the tests"     answer one task, print the result, and exit
  dsh --profile tui --patch ./extra.yml      boot a custom profile with one extra overlay
  dsh --profile tui --resume <session>       arguments after the launcher flags reach the app
  dsh --profile web --help                   the web app's own flags and help
  dsh plugin --profile tui add <package>     install a plugin into the tui profile

capability_table.capability: launcher boot of acp profile in probe-private home
capability_table.documented: `dsh --profile acp` starts the shipped stdio server
capability_table.conclusion: the launcher initializes the shipped template into a probe-private DSH_HOME; no prompt sent, so no inference

capability_table.capability: acpx custom agent via structured argv on Windows
capability_table.documented: custom agent registry; raw command strings rejected on win32
capability_table.local_observation: `--agent "<command string>"` rejected on win32 with an explicit argv-array error; `agents.<name>.argv` config path also probed by the acpx CLI
capability_table.live: argv agent launched the real DSH (see live rows)
capability_table.conclusion: the structured argv boundary works on Windows; the one-string form does not

capability_table.documented: ACP initialize negotiates version and capabilities
capability_table.conclusion: verified against both mock and real DSH

capability_table.documented: session/new then session/prompt returns a stopReason
capability_table.conclusion: mock and real DSH both produce a stopReason
update kinds observed live: see the prompt-turn row

capability_table.documented: exit code 0 when the task completed, 1 when it aborted or errored
capability_table.mock: exit=0 on success; exit=1 on error
capability_table.conclusion: exit status distinguishes success from failure in both layers

capability_table.mock: unknown-method exit=1; garbage-line exit=0; bad-init exit=0
capability_table.conclusion: an explicit JSON-RPC error fails the run; a malformed initialize *response* was accepted and the turn continued, so this client does not validate that handshake shape

capability_table.documented: client must report failure rather than hang
capability_table.conclusion: client reports a failure instead of blocking
bounded wait with an explicit timeout error

capability_table.documented: cooperative session/cancel; acpx cancel / prompt-owned cancellation
capability_table.mock: not observed: sending CTRL_BREAK to the client killed it (exit 0xC000013A) before any session/cancel reached the agent
capability_table.conclusion: NOT VERIFIED - the cooperative cancel path was never exercised; a hard client stop is not evidence of cancellation capability
